evidence.methodology_note: Assigned languages for this work unit = Kotlin only; per multi-language Ecosystem sharding, only the Kotlin key is populated for each metric and the runner is expected to merge disjoint per-language shards from sibling workers. Rubrics above are declared as the frozen, language-neutral scoring definitions intended for uniform application to all 10 languages by whichever workers cover them; this worker applied them only to Kotlin per its assignment.

citations: Official Gradle Kotlin plugin (org.jetbrains.kotlin.jvm.gradle.plugin, last released Jul 15 2026) and official Maven plugin (org.jetbrains.kotlin/kotlin-maven-plugin) both exist as first-party JetBrains artifacts under org.jetbrains.kotlin, satisfying C1.

kotlinlang.org's own tutorial shows a Kotlin project wiring kotlin("test") plus JUnit Jupiter directly into Gradle's tasks.test { useJUnitPlatform() }, and a parallel pom.xml/Maven configuration, demonstrating C2/C3 out-of-the-box discovery.
kotlinlang.org hosts an official tutorial: 'Kotlin/JVM supports the latest stable JUnit version, JUnit 6' with a version catalog entry, satisfying C3.

Kotest ships a dedicated Gradle plugin (io.kotest) runnable via './gradlew kotest' or from IntelliJ's Gradle -> tasks -> verification -> kotest task, but the plugin's own README calls it alpha, and Android JUnit5 plugins are Android-scoped, so C4 is docked slightly (18/20).

The Kotlin Koans workshop repository documents running tests 'on the Gradle tool window (View | Tool Windows | Gradle)' inside IntelliJ IDEA, confirming IDE/build-tool test-runner integration (C5); Maven test-phase integration is also documented, but no equivalent first-party coverage/report-merging tool was confirmed in this pass, so C5 is docked slightly (18/20).

components: C1 (20pts): First-party/official build-tool plugin(s) exist for 2+ mainstream build systems (full=20, one system=10, none/community-only=0).
C2 (20pts): A bundled/native unit-test mechanism runs via a single standard build-tool command with automatic test discovery, no extra glue code (full=20, requires manual wiring=10, unsupported=0).
C3 (20pts): Official documentation provides first-party tutorial/support for the ecosystem's dominant general-purpose test framework (full=20, partial/community-only=10, none=0).
C4 (20pts): 2+ alternative/specialized test frameworks (property-based, BDD-style, etc.) ship with dedicated build-tool plugins/tasks (full=20, one such framework=10, none=0).
C5 (20pts): Test results integrate into the build tool's task graph and the mainstream IDE's test runner without extra configuration (full=20, partial=10, none=0).
rubric.description: Frozen 5-component rubric (20 pts each, sum to 0-100), applied identically to all 10 languages by the Ecosystem evaluation. Same evidence sources (official language site, official build-tool plugin registries, official docs), same query rules, and same conversion apply unchanged across languages.

citations: kotlinlang.org's 'Learning materials overview' officially indexes basic syntax, a full Kotlin tour, idioms guides, and Java-to-Kotlin migration guides for strings, collections, and nullability, satisfying C1.

Dokka is described by kotlinlang.org itself as 'an API documentation engine for Kotlin' that 'understands Kotlin's KDoc comments and Java's Javadoc comments' and is applied as an official Gradle plugin (id("org.jetbrains.dokka")) or Maven plugin, satisfying C2; it is used by major libraries such as kotlinx.coroutines, Ktor, and OkHttp for their API reference docs.

The official learning-materials page lists Kotlin Koans ('complete exercises to learn the Kotlin syntax' where 'each exercise is created as a failing unit test'), the Kotlin Core track by JetBrains Academy, hands-on tutorials, and a Coursera course, satisfying C3.

Official documentation pages show recent maintenance activity, e.g. the KDoc reference page dated August 12, 2026, the JUnit testing tutorial dated December 18, 2025 noting current JUnit 6 support, and the learning-materials overview dated September 3, 2025, supporting C4 (slightly docked since no explicit versioned release-note cadence for docs was independently verified).

A broad third-party documentation ecosystem is readily observable, including Baeldung's Dokka introduction, and multiple independent tutorial sites (dev.to, Petri Kainulainen, Tom Gregory, lastminute.com/technology) covering Kotlin build/test configuration, satisfying C5 (slightly docked since this is a sampled snapshot rather than an exhaustive community-doc audit).

components: C1 (20pts): A comprehensive, structured official language reference/documentation portal exists and covers syntax, idioms, and migration guidance (full=20, partial=10, none=0).
C2 (20pts): A first-party API-documentation generator exists and integrates with the language's official build tools (full=20, third-party-only=10, none=0).
C3 (20pts): Official, structured, interactive learning materials for newcomers exist (exercises, guided tours, courses) (full=20, partial=10, none=0).
C4 (20pts): Documentation is actively/recently maintained, evidenced by recent publish/update timestamps on official pages (full=20, stale/no evidence=0-10).
C5 (20pts): A visible third-party/community documentation ecosystem supplements the official docs (tutorial sites, Q&A, blogs) (full=20, sparse=10, none=0).

snapshot_and_sources.selection_rule: Official JetBrains-maintained (kotlinlang.org, github.com/Kotlin, JetBrains-namespaced Maven/Gradle plugin coordinates) sources were prioritized as the deterministic external selection rule for a first-party/official-ecosystem language; independent third-party tutorial sites were sampled only to evidence the community-documentation sub-component (C5) and not used as standalone proxies.
